desc: Scraper made from a shell, cut into a square, and lashed to a folded, rough cloth, and used to remove outer layers from bast of paper mulberry. The scraper is part of a collection of kapa tools used to make barkcloth, and was made specifically for the U.S. Exploring Expedition conservation project that took place in the Department of Anthropology Conservation Lab at the Museum Support Center in 2012-2013. The scraper was made by Daniel Richard Jonathan Kapalikuokalani Maile of Kaimuki, Oahu, age 25, a Masters candidate at UH Manoa-Pacific Island Studies.
